text.tspan: Types are checked, then ERASED. Nothing you write in a type annotation survives to run time.
interface User { id: number; name: string }
The interface vanished entirely: an interface is a compile-time shape, not an object.
So you cannot test a type with typeof or instanceof, and data crossing the boundary
(JSON from a server, a form field, localStorage) is NOT checked. Validate it yourself.
Why bother, then? Because the check happens BEFORE you ship: a typo, a wrong argument order, or a forgotten null is a red
squiggle in the editor instead of a bug in production. TypeScript is a superset: every valid .js file is already valid .ts.
In this course we run .ts straight through tsx, which strips the types without type-checking; tsc --noEmit does the checking.
